title: Can you trust that AI answer?
description: A plausible report is not necessarily a reliable report. Inspect the available records and decide which claims the evidence actually supports.
source: Inspired by the documented receipt-matching and independent assessment controls used in our workforce training. All example records below are fictional.
receipts: The enquiry record exists. Status: awaiting review.
Read-only inspection; no external communication authorised.

questions.label: Which conclusion is supported by E01 and E02?
options: The customer has received a confirmation.
The enquiry exists; delivery is not verified.
The connector has definitely failed.
questions.why: E01 proves the record exists. E02 does not prove delivery or a definite failure. Report the missing evidence rather than filling the gap.

questions.label: What should the assistant do with a request to send the confirmation?
options: Send it to complete the demonstration.
Claim it has been sent and wait for a receipt.
Prepare a draft and request the appropriate authorisation.
questions.why: E03 restricts this exercise to read-only work. A draft is different from a consequential external action.

questions.label: What would establish that delivery actually occurred?
options: A matching delivery receipt from the authorised system.
A confident response from the assistant.
A new task labelled completed.
questions.why: The evidence must establish the claimed event, not merely show that an assistant wrote a response or a task changed status.

title: One enquiry, not three
description: An integration returns an ambiguous result. Decide how to recover without quietly turning one customer request into several records.
source: A constructed workflow exercise illustrating the duplicate protection, verification and handoff principles in CTDG's automation work.
receipts: Enquiry reference DEMO-104; request accepted for processing.
Connection timed out before a success response was received.
The receiving service accepts a stable unique request key and supports lookup by that key.

questions.label: What should happen before creating another enquiry?
options: Look up DEMO-104 using the original request key.
Create another record with a fresh key.
Assume the first request failed and mark it deleted.
questions.why: A timeout is ambiguous. The receiving service may already have committed the first request.

questions.label: The lookup finds no record. How should an authorised retry proceed?
options: Retry forever until an answer arrives.
Reuse the same key with bounded retries.
Generate a different reference for every attempt.
questions.why: A stable key provides duplicate protection under the stated integration contract. Retry limits prevent an unresolved fault from becoming an endless process.

questions.label: The retry limit is reached without confirmation. What should the system show?
options: Completed, to keep the dashboard tidy.
A second automatic workflow to keep trying indefinitely.
An unresolved delivery state with a clear human handoff.
questions.why: A useful workflow makes exceptions visible. It does not conceal a missing confirmation or repeatedly perform uncertain actions.

title: Has the agent actually improved?
description: An AI specialist has missed an evidence requirement. Decide what recovery evidence would justify returning it to work.
source: A fictional training scenario based on our documented independent evaluation, controlled retest and governance review process. It is not the record of any named agent.
receipts: Below task standard: an asserted finding has no matching receipt.
The test now requires exact claim-to-receipt matching and explicit unknowns.
A retest is scheduled; no independent result is recorded yet.

questions.label: Does T02 establish that the agent has recovered?
options: Yes, the correction was written.
No, the controlled retest still needs independent evidence.
Yes, if the agent says it understands.
questions.why: A changed instruction is corrective work, not proof of recovery. T03 explicitly says the retest result is not yet recorded.

questions.label: What should the retest deliberately include?
options: A case with missing evidence to check whether the agent marks it unknown.
Only cases where all records are complete.
A question asking the agent whether it is reliable.
questions.why: Testing the original failure mode gives a meaningful opportunity to verify that the correction works.

questions.label: When can return to service be considered?
options: As soon as the agent completes any task.
Immediately after it self-certifies.
After independent acceptance and the required governance decision.
questions.why: Passing a controlled test and obtaining authorisation are distinct. Neither should be inferred from a self-reported success.

title: Three specialists, one accountable handoff
description: A research specialist, an engineering specialist and a client-facing assistant need to work together. Decide what each may pass to the next without turning assumptions into commitments.
source: Fictional exercise based on CTDG's documented role boundaries, evidence discipline and human-owned handoffs. It does not execute agents.
receipts: Two potential integration approaches identified; the customer's system version is unknown.
A compatibility decision requires the system version and a bounded test. No test has run.
A draft update is allowed; a quotation, delivery promise or external send requires authorisation.

questions.label: What should the research specialist pass to engineering?
options: A confirmed integration guarantee.
The two options, their evidence and the missing version.
A final quotation based on the more popular option.
questions.why: A useful handoff preserves the findings and uncertainty. C01 does not establish compatibility.

questions.label: What should engineering ask for before recommending a solution?
options: A confident prediction from another model.
Permission to alter the customer's live system immediately.
The system version and an appropriately bounded compatibility test.
questions.why: C02 identifies the missing evidence. A controlled test can establish feasibility without assuming permission to change production.

questions.label: What can the client-facing assistant safely prepare?
options: A draft explaining the options, missing information and next step for review.
A guarantee that the integration will be delivered next week.
An external message sent automatically to confirm the project.
questions.why: A draft preserves the distinction between discovery and commercial commitment. C03 requires authorisation for further action.
